question: Using Wang et al. 2025 virtual brain twin data (simulated Patients 1 and 2, VBT_INS_Stimulation), can a qualified virtual-brain pipeline recover the epileptogenic zone (EZ) of a held-out virtual patient from its SEEG, and which virtual intervention (resection/ablation of the estimated zone or electrical stimulation) most reduces simulated seizure spread, judged against the hidden ground truth?
intended_use: Methods research on virtual (simulated) patients. No real patient is involved; nothing here is a clinical recommendation.
population: Two virtual patients with focal epilepsy from Wang et al. 2025 (repo HuifangWang/VBT_INS_Stimulation @ 5367ef4): each has a 162-region VEP-atlas structural connectome, an SEEG gain matrix and simulated SEEG/EEG under SEEG and temporal-interference (TI) stimulation. Plus synthetic cases generated by R3 for benchmarking.
inclusion_rules: Data: only files of the pinned repo commit 5367ef4 (data/dataSim/*, data/EMF/*, data/*_stimulation.xlsx, examples/*.ipynb) and locally generated synthetic data. Every file is hashed in a retrieval manifest.
Test patient: Wang Patient 2 (P2), using P2_SEEG_ts_fit.npz (SEEG time series, SC, gain). Development patient: Wang Patient 1 (P1), used for the synthetic qualification benchmark only.

Ground truth for P2 = the generating parameters (x0 map / EZ and propagation-zone regions) that the authors' simulation notebooks set for Patient 2. R2 extracts it into a separate file that LEAD seals in the vault before any R3 task starts. If it cannot be extracted unambiguously, the authors' published P2 posterior (Patient2_*_stimulation.xlsx) is sealed instead as a reference standard and the endpoint is reported as 'agreement with authors', not 'recovery of truth'.

Modeling basis: vep-stim (Wang 2025) Stan inversion, with the study-001 defects fixed (likelihood skip, per-file sampling rate, padding) and the study-001 failure causes addressed (observation model for autocorrelated noise, data-centred offset/amplitude priors, multi-start sampling). Every patch lives in a work-dir copy with its diff recorded.

Virtual interventions (R4): (a) resection/ablation of the estimated EZ (node excitability set to healthy and/or node disconnected); (b) SEEG-contact electrical stimulation modeled as a gain-weighted stimulus at chosen contacts (Wang-style spatial weighting), with the therapeutic form (e.g. sustained inhibitory current or high-frequency pulse train) prespecified by R4 before simulation; (c) TI stimulation using the authors' EMF field maps where a region mapping is feasible, otherwise reported as infeasible.
exclusion_rules: No real-patient data in this study.

R3 and R4 must not open the authors' simulation notebooks (examples/Sim_*.ipynb), the stimulation-posterior spreadsheets (data/*_stimulation.xlsx) or any study-001 work file that records P2 generating values. These are reserved for R2 (extraction), the vault and R5 outcome evaluation.

endpoints.qualification: Synthetic benchmark through the full pipeline (raw-like signals -> features -> likelihood) on P1's connectome and gain: planted EZ ranked 1st by posterior x0, x0 R-hat < 1.05 for every region, false positives reported.
endpoints.primary_ez_recovery: On P2 (blinded): rank of each true EZ region, precision and recall of the estimated EZ set (regions with P(x0 > threshold) > 0.5), with posterior uncertainty.
endpoints.intervention_effect_model: Per candidate intervention on the fitted P2 model: change in number of seizing regions and in seizure duration vs a paired no-intervention baseline, per posterior sample (median and 90% interval).
endpoints.intervention_effect_truth: The same candidate interventions applied to the sealed ground-truth P2 model by R5 after predictions are frozen; concordance of the candidate ranking (model vs truth) and the true effect of the model-chosen candidate.
endpoints.signals: Simulated SEEG before and after each intervention is stored for the report.

follow_up: Simulation horizon prespecified by R4 (same for baseline and every candidate).

development: P1 (and synthetic cases derived from P1)
split_rules.label_access: P2 ground truth sealed in the vault before modeling; only the R5 outcome_evaluation task may reveal it, after predictions (ModelBundle EZ estimate + R4 candidate ranking) are frozen.
split_rules.leakage_controls: Disclosed exposure: in study-001 the R3 and R5 agents read the authors' notebooks, and a study-001 log line records that the P2 simulations used EZ x0 -2.2/-2.3 (without region names). Study-002 agents start fresh and are told not to read study-001 work files; any residual exposure is reported.

metrics: Qualification: x0 R-hat, bulk/tail ESS, divergences, tree depth; planted-EZ rank and P(rank 1); false-positive count.
EZ recovery on P2: true-EZ ranks, precision, recall, P(rank 1) for each true EZ region.
Interventions: paired difference in seizing-region count and seizure duration (median, 90% interval over posterior samples); candidate ranking stability across samples.
Truth check: Spearman/Kendall concordance of candidate rankings (model vs truth) and regret of the model-chosen candidate.

acceptance_criteria.model_bundle: Convergence passes (all x0 R-hat < 1.05, no unexplained divergences) and the synthetic benchmark recovers the planted EZ (rank 1). If the benchmark fails, P2 fitting does not proceed and the arm is reported as not qualified.
acceptance_criteria.simulation_batch: Paired baselines present, seeds recorded, numerical checks pass, same horizon for all candidates.
acceptance_criteria.outcome_evaluation: Predictions frozen before reveal; metrics computed exactly as specified.

budgets.per_fit_compute: 3 hours wall clock per R3 fitting task

approvals_required: Download from the pinned repo (Apache-2.0, ~21 MB): data/dataSim (8 npz, 17.4 MB), data/EMF (4 mgh, 0.2 MB), data/*_stimulation.xlsx (0.4 MB), and the simulation/plotting notebooks Sim_SEEG_nf*, Sim_TI_nf, compute_TI_envelope, stimulation_plot_time_series_* (~3 MB). The three 7-8 MB run_samplings notebooks are not downloaded.
Install nilearn into .venv-model (bundled fsaverage5 brain surfaces for the 3D figure; ~10 MB, BSD).
